papers.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
papers.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multi-omics - metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides - across 1,543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multi-omic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune/repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

papers.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
papers.abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly two weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstruct a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantify clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell-type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

papers.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. papers.title: A fluctuation test for gastruloid heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Organoids grown side by side under identical conditions vary unpredictably, a longstanding obstacle to their use. Adapting the logic of a classic fluctuation test to gastruloids grown from single stem cells shows that this variability is largely inherited rather than induced and is traceable to fluctuations in the state of the founding cell.

papers.title: Arabidopsis uses distinct coumarins and bacterial pathways for pH-adaptive iron acquisition
papers.abstract: Arabidopsis coordinates Fe acquisition with its root microbiota by releasing distinct coumarin chemotypes in response to environmental pH. These root-exuded specialized metabolites interact with root-associated bacteria to mobilize Fe either through bacterial siderophore-dependent chelation at circumneutral pH or through bacterial redox-sensing-controlled reduction at acidic pH.

papers.title: Immunoregulatory gene GIMAP6 suppresses lethal atherosclerotic vasculopathy and ischemic heart failure
papers.abstract: By destabilizing the endothelium and promoting macrophage lipid loading and inflammation, GIMAP6 deficiency drives atherosclerosis and ischemic heart disease through a mechanism that operates without hyperlipidemia, yet hyperlipidemia significantly exacerbates disease progression.

papers.title: Comprehensive lineage tracing maps the landscape of cell fate decisions in mouse embryogenesis
papers.abstract: We use PEtracer to reconstruct high-resolution lineage histories for >1.4 million cells from E7.5 to E10.0 during mouse development, providing a quantitative view of fate bias, restriction timing, and clonal output. Across diverse tissues, these data reveal highly reproducible lineage architectures and define general and tissue-specific strategies of cell fate specification.

papers.title: Microglia-mediated extracellular matrix disruption drives neuronal dysfunction, motor impairments, and sedation following alcohol abuse
papers.abstract: Alcohol’s brain effects are attributed to neurons, leaving microglial functional involvement untested. Paouri, Stanko, et al. show that microglia drive alcohol-induced sedation, motor impairment, and synaptic and neuronal loss through MyD88-dependent perisynaptic extracellular matrix (ECM) disruption. Equivalent neuron-targeted sedation bypassing microglia spares the ECM. Brain ECM loss also marks human alcohol use disorder, identifying a therapeutic target distinct from neuronal interventions.

papers.title: Spatial omics resolves adrenergic and mesenchymal cell states in neuroblastoma
papers.abstract: Patel et al. combine six spatial-omics platforms with single-cell/single-nucleus RNA sequencing across 54 neuroblastoma tumors to resolve a debate over malignant mesenchymal (MES) tumor cells. Using signatures from patient-derived xenografts, they identify MES tumor cells and show that a higher MES score predicts worse patient outcome.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into chromatin modulation by the “orphan” remodeler ATRX
papers.abstract: Duan et al. solved the structure of ATRX ATPase-nucleosome complex, uncovering three distinctive features that enable ATRX to remodel nucleosomes. These newly identified features are indispensable for protecting cells from G4 stress. The work provides a framework for interpreting both known and future mutations linked to ATRX-related disorders.

papers.title: Introgression catalyzing plumage evolution and speciation in an Asian songbird complex
papers.abstract: Jiang et al. combine a chromosome-level genome with population resequencing to show that adaptive introgression from a parapatric outgroup species explains genomic divergence between two Asian sister songbirds. The introgressed regions harbor melanin synthesis genes, revealing how introgression can promote plumage evolution and speciation.

papers.title: Host-triggered prophage induction drives Lactiplantibacillus plantarum symbiosis through bacterial lysis
papers.abstract: Zhu et al. show that pp2 prophage of LpNC8, a Drosophila symbiont, promotes bacterial lysis and the recovery of extracellular vesicles containing lipoteichoic acids, supporting juvenile growth under nutritional stress. The copper cell region of the fly midgut promotes prophage activity in vivo, linking intestinal physiology to bacterial lysis and symbiotic function.

papers.title: Inferring binding specificities of human transcription factors with the wisdom of crowds
papers.abstract: Gryzunov et al. report IBIS, the largest open community benchmark for inferring human transcription factor binding specificities from five experimental platforms. Deep learning models outperform classical position weight matrices only slightly and only if properly designed. The released datasets, protocols, and models provide a versatile framework for future benchmarking.

papers.title: Mapping the functional dark proteome in cancer
papers.abstract: A generation after the genomics revolution, and with the advent of proteomic technologies, the dark proteome now stands as a potential new direction for cancer science and therapeutics. The dark proteome covers a vast terrain of previously undiscovered and uncharacterized protein molecules derived from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. Over the past decade, an unprecedented depth of resolution of the dark proteome has been attained, identifying diverse classes of dark proteins with thousands of members each. Increasingly, individual dark proteins are also being characterized as functional components of cancer cell biology as well as potential therapeutic targets. Therefore, as a whole, the dark proteome offers the possibility to advance cancer science, diagnosis and treatment. Yet, many fundamental questions about the dark proteome remain, including key gaps in knowledge regarding its regulation, contribution to cancer phenotypes and antigenicity, and tractability for clinical-grade therapies. This Perspective outlines the current state of knowledge of the dark proteome in cancer, highlighting critical areas in which further research is needed. Furthermore, it poses guiding questions that illuminate important directions of growth for the field of the cancer dark proteome. The dark proteome encompasses previously undiscovered and uncharacterized protein molecules derived from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. In this Perspective, Prensner et al. describe the current understanding of the dark proteome and set out the critical questions that need to be addressed in the field to determine whether the dark proteome can fulfill its potential for clinical translation.

papers.title: Epigenome Alterations and 3D Chromatin Architecture Remodeling in Inflammatory Macrophage Activation under Diabetic Conditions
papers.abstract: Aberrant monocyte/macrophage activation in diabetes drives chronic inflammation and diabetic complications. Although epigenetic mechanisms are implicated in these processes, the contribution of three-dimensional (3D) chromatin reorganization remains unclear. Here, we use integrated multi-omics approaches to profile gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D chromatin architecture in human CD14 monocyte-derived macrophages exposed to high glucose and TNF- (HT), mimicking the diabetic milieu. HT induces inflammatory transcription programs that recapitulate those observed in diabetes and dynamically remodel chromatin accessibility, enhancer-promoter interactions, and topologically associated domains. Inflammatory genes exhibit increased chromatin accessibility, whereas cell cycle and metabolic genes display reduced accessibility and weakened enhancer-promoter interactions. These architectural changes promote the convergence of lineage-determining and signal-dependent transcription factors at enhancer-promoter loops, generating distinct regulatory hubs that orchestrate pro-inflammatory responses. Similar enhancer-promoter interactions are observed in peripheral blood derived monocytes from individuals with diabetes. Furthermore, perturbing chromatin interactions via CRISPR interference targeting HT-induced enhancers suppresses nearby CCL2 and other chemokine genes. Collectively, this first comprehensive enhancer connectome map of macrophages under diabetic conditions advances the field by revealing extensive disease-associated rewiring of the 3D epigenome, highlighting chromatin architecture and epigenetic mechanisms as potential therapeutic target for diabetes-associated inflammation.
affiliations: Beckman Research Institute of the City of Hope (corresponding author)

papers.title: Integrative Multi-omics Analysis of the Human Skeletal Muscle Response to Endurance or Resistance Exercise: Findings from the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC)
papers.abstract: The Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC) was established to systematically characterize the molecular basis of the health benefits of exercise. Here, we present the integrative, multi-omics response of human skeletal muscle to acute endurance (EE) and resistance (RE) exercise. Distinct temporal responses were observed, with changes in ATAC-seq, phosphoproteome, and metabolome occurring before changes in the transcriptome and proteome. These distinct temporal multi-omic dynamics were used to identify transcriptional regulatory hubs converging around MEF2A and NFIC regulation of autophagy, angiogenesis and metabolism. Further, early RE-specific phosphoproteome signatures counteracted epigenetic modifications and downregulated transcripts involved in protein turnover. Additional findings include suppression of HIPK2/3 kinase signatures linked to the acute exercise regulation of sarcomeric proteins TTN, NEB, ANKRD2 and LMOD2. Our data demonstrate distinct temporal regulation across the multi-omic landscape of human skeletal muscle, with EE and RE eliciting common and unique molecular signatures.
affiliations: Proteomics Platform, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA (corresponding author)

papers.title: AXIS: Agentic Extraction and Integration of Simulation Scenarios for Quantitative Systems Pharmacology
papers.abstract: Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) models are executable and mechanistic representations of biological systems that are increasingly used to design, evaluate, and help enrich clinical trials. Reusing a published model, however, requires knowing what each entity represents biologically (often inferable only from its relations to other entities) and what value it must take for a given scenario, information carried in the accompanying publication, not the model file. Agentic systems automate simulation setup from user-specified tasks over standardized parameter sets. In parallel, literature-mining tools extract reported quantities from publications. However, closing the loop, going from paper and model to an executable configuration that reproduces the published result, remains a manual curation task. Here, we present AXIS, a modular multi-agent framework that converts a published QSP model together with its companion publication into simulation-ready configurations. The framework integrates dependency-aware entity grounding, evidence-linked scenario extraction, semantic and structural entity search, sandboxed deterministic computation, and expert input on ambiguity. AXIS comprises three modules that ground the model's entities, recover the scenarios described in the paper, and resolve each into concrete parameter assignments. We demonstrate the framework end-to-end on a published disease model, reconstructing the figure reported in its companion publication. AXIS recovers the reported scenarios, produces parameter assignments matching an expert-curated ground truth, and defers to an expert where a required quantity appears in neither source.
