papers.title: RuPHOTACs provide photocontrol over protein degradation with optimized properties for biological applications
papers.abstract: PROteolysis TArgeting Chimeras (PROTACs) are bifunctional molecules that catalyze degradation of selected proteins by inducing protein:protein interactions (PPIs) between E3 ubiquitin ligases and the protein of interest. A critical limitation is undesired effects in untargeted tissues, necessitating approaches to impose spatiotemporal control over PROTAC function. Here we present Ru(II) photocages that can be released with low energy light, providing triggered PROTAC activity on demand. The systems, termed Ruthenium-based PHOToActivated Chimeras (RuPHOTACs), were validated by targeting bromodomain-containing proteins, which act as crucial epigenetic regulators, and also strongly reduced levels of c-MYC and PIM1. RuPHOTACs demonstrate that the incorporation of metal components within organic PROTACs confers multiple advantages for light-controlled systems for chemical biology applications, including the highest selectivity for activation in the light vs. the dark, improved potency against the target proteins of interest, and increased efficacy in vivo using low energy red light. To efficiently monitor protein degradation via optical means, a strategy was implemented by creating a fusion of a photoconvertible protein, Dendra2, with the proteins of interest. This bifunctional reporter system for live cell analysis decouples protein degradation efficiency and rates from signals arising from new protein production, and is superior to prior reporter systems described for PROTACs because it directly measures the true degradation rate of the target protein in intact, viable cells while simultaneously tracking newly synthesized protein without perturbing translation, proteostasis, or cell health. PROTACs offer a powerful strategy to eliminate disease-relevant proteins, but off-target activity in healthy tissues remains a major challenge. Here, the authors introduce Ruthenium-based PHOToActivated Chimeras (RuPHOTACs), a new class of light-responsive PROTACs that remain inactive until triggered by low-energy light.

papers.title: Powder-to-membrane transformation affording 2D/3D COF membranes for molecular separations
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of reticular chemistry has enabled the synthesis of thousands of covalent organic framework (COF) powders bearing various structures and functions. Nevertheless, processing these COF powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a dynamic covalent chemistry-based dual-drive strategy is harnessed to drive macroscopic structural variation, achieving the transformation of powdered COFs into defect-free COF membranes. This powder-to-membrane transformation is enabled by the internal factor of framework reconstruction and the external driving force of acid attack, showcasing high processibility, which affords scalable two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) COF membranes with a maximum area of 225 cm2. The optimum TpPa membrane demonstrates excellent performance in molecular sieving, displaying high rejections towards dye (99%) and pharmaceutical molecules (98%) and a pure water permeance of 179.0 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Moreover, our dual-drive transformation outperforms conventional methods in fabrication efficiency, conversion ratio, separation performance, etc., offering a green, efficient, versatile, and scalable strategy for the preparation and application of COF membranes in chemical engineering separations. Processing covalent organic framework (COF) powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains challenging. Here, the authors demonstrate a dual-drive strategy that drives macroscopic structural variation and transforms COF powders into defect-free membranes.

papers.title: Magnetic Electroluminescent response as a predictive indicator of operational lifetime in phosphorescent blue OLEDs
papers.abstract: Improving operational lifetime remains a major challenge for blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) harvesting triplet excitons. Achieving substantial lifetime enhancement requires analytical techniques that elucidate degradation mechanisms. Because conventional lifetime analysis involves destructive aging tests, developing non-invasive methods that correlate strongly with device longevity is highly desirable. Here, we show that the operational lifetime of blue phosphorescent OLEDs quantitatively correlates with the electroluminescence (EL) response under magnetic fields. This behavior is explained by a magneto-EL response function that reflects degradation-sensitive spin-pair kinetics under magnetic fields. A strong linear correlation (confidence > 95%) is identified between the magneto-EL response strength (fMEL) and device lifetime, with longer-operable OLEDs exhibiting lower fMEL values. These findings establish a non-destructive approach for analyzing and predicting the stability of blue phosphorescent OLEDs. Predicting the operational lifetime of blue organic light-emitting diodes without destructive and lengthy aging tests remains challenging. Ji et al. identify a magnetic-field electroluminescence response that quantitatively predicts operational lifetime.

papers.title: WeedNet: a foundation model-based global-to-local AI approach for weed species identification and classification
papers.abstract: Early weed identification is crucial for effective management and control, and researchers, agronomists, and technology developers are increasingly interested in automating this process using computer vision and artificial intelligence; however, limited expert-verified data and variable morphological features have hindered the development of AI-based weed identification models. To address these issues, we present WeedNet, a global-scale weed identification model that can recognize an extensive set of weed species. WeedNet is an end-to-end weed identification pipeline that uses self-supervised learning, fine-tuning, and enhanced trustworthiness strategies. WeedNet achieved 91.02% accuracy across 1,593 weed species, with 41% of species achieving 100% accuracy. Using a fine-tuning approach, the local Iowa WeedNet model achieved 97.38% overall accuracy for 84 Iowa weeds. Testing across intra-species dissimilarity and inter-species similarity suggests that diversity in the images collected, spanning all the growth stages and distinguishable plant characteristics, is crucial in driving model performance. The global WeedNet model serves as a foundation, and the global-to-local strategy enables targeted fine-tuning to improve performance in regional weed communities. Additional validation of drone- and ground-rover-based images highlights WeedNet’s potential for integration into robotic platforms. Furthermore, integration with artificial intelligence for conversational use provides intelligent agricultural and ecological conservation consulting tools for farmers, researchers, and government agencies across diverse landscapes. Weeds consistently threaten crop yields worldwide, making early and accurate identification essential for effective management. Trained on 14 million images representing 1,593 weed species, WeedNet achieved 91% global accuracy and, through global-to-local fine-tuning, reached 97% accuracy for Iowa weeds.

papers.title: Repurposing Cas12a2-mediated abortive infection for efficient and low-toxicity microbial genome editing
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas systems have revolutionized microbial genome engineering, yet counter-selection strategies typically rely on targeted DNA cleavage, where the severe cytotoxicity of double-strand breaks restricts transformation efficiency and clonal recovery. Here, we present an innovative strategy, SuCas12a2-Universal Recombination Editing (SURE), that circumvents these limitations by repurposing the RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas12a2 system. Instead of directly attacking the genome, SURE utilizes Cas12a2’s RNA-triggered collateral activity to induce an abortive infection-like state, providing a potent yet recoverable selective pressure. This strategy increases transformation efficiency by up to 1,000-fold compared to Cas9- or Cas12-based systems while achieving over 90% editing efficiency for gene knockout, insertion, and replacement in Escherichia coli MG1655. We validate the SURE platform’s broad utility by extending it to diverse species, including Bacillus subtilis BSZR and Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Mechanistically, we identify collateral double-stranded DNA degradation as the decisive factor for driving efficient selection. Finally, we apply this system to engineer E. coli MG1655 for efficient assimilation of the plastic monomer ethylene glycol, demonstrating its practical utility. Collectively, this work establishes a universal and robust RNA-guided editing framework that resolves the toxicity-efficiency trade-off inherent to the conventional DNA-targeting methods. Microbial genome engineering is often limited by toxicity from existing selection methods. Here, the authors develop a Cas12a2-based RNA-guided editing strategy that improves efficiency and reduces cellular damage, providing a robust tool for microbial engineering.

papers.title: A Robust Gel Polymer Electrode with Controlled-Release Polymerization towards Practical Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract: While rational electrode engineering has promoted the kinetics of lithium-sulfur batteries, persistent lithium polysulfide diffusion continues to undermine the cyclability of conventional liquid electrolyte systems. We propose a quasi-solid gel electrode design that integrates the sulfur species-blocking attributes of a solid-state system within a liquid electrolyte framework. This is achieved through a well-designed free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy, which precisely governs the formation of a processable poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. This approach enables secondary in situ gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration, forming gel-phase electrode architectures. Mechanistically, the resulting gel-based electrode provides dynamically adaptive stress dissipation to accommodate volume variations, establishes continuous ion-permeable pathways for deeper positive electrode discharge, and acts as a synergistic physico-chemical barrier for sulfur species confinement. As a result, the positive electrode delivers a high initial capacity of 812.8 mA h g–1 at 2 C and sustains stable cycling operation over 1000 cycles. A 1.7 Ah-level pouch cell demonstrates potential for a sustained power supply for an unmanned aerial vehicle. A free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy precisely governs the formation of poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. Secondary gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration leads to the effective enhancement of lithium-sulfur batteries.

papers.title: Intravenous hyaluronidase-expressing oncolytic adenovirus with chemotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer: a randomized phase 2b trial
papers.abstract: Zabilugene almadenorepvec (VCN-01) is a hyaluronidase-expressing oncolytic adenovirus with a favorable safety profile and encouraging antitumor activity in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. This randomized phase 2b trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of two doses of intravenous VCN-01 with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) versus GnP alone as first-line therapy in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) in the intent-to-treat and full analysis set (FAS) populations, and safety and tolerability in the safety population. In the intent-to-treat population (VCN-01 + GnP, n = 53; GnP, n = 48), median OS in the VCN-01 + GnP versus GnP group was 10.6 versus 8.6 months (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.69 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.42–1.12), P = 0.196) and progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 4.6 months (HR = 0.63 (95% CI 0.4–1.00), P = 0.046). In the FAS population (n = 48 per group), median OS was 10.8 months in the VCN-01 + GnP group versus 8.6 months in the GnP group (HR = 0.57 (95% CI 0.34-0.96), P = 0.055) and progression-free survival was 7.0 versus 4.6 months (HR = 0.55 (95% CI, 0.34-0.88), P = 0.011). The primary efficacy endpoint of OS was met in the FAS population. Duration of response was 11.2 versus 5.4 months (HR = 0.22 (95% CI 0.08–0.63), P = 0.004). No statistically significant differences were observed in overall response rate, disease control rate or carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels between treatment groups. In addition, survival rates in the VCN-01 + GnP group versus the GnP group were 35.5% versus 12.8% at 15 months, and 31.1% versus 8.5% at 18 months. Patients receiving two VCN-01 doses 14 weeks apart showed greater survival benefit, with sustained circulating viral genomes indicating ongoing viral replication and preserved second-dose bioactivity despite persistent neutralizing antibodies. More frequent VCN-01-related events included pyrexia, flu-like symptoms, elevation in liver enzymes and decreases in platelet counts, with serious events occurring in 22.6% of patients. Milder toxicity was observed after the second administration. Two fatal events occurred, one in each treatment group; neither was considered related to study treatment. These results further support VCN-01 combined with GnP as a first-line therapy for metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and warrant evaluation in a blinded phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05673811 . In the randomized phase 2b VIRAGE trial, patients with treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic cancer received the hyaluronidase-expressing oncolytic adenovirus zabilugene almadenorepvec (VCN-01) intravenously with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) or GnP alone, showing that VCN-01 plus GnP led to prolonged overall survival.

papers.title: Global, site-resolved analysis of ubiquitylation occupancy and turnover rate reveals systems properties
Salicylic acid engages central metabolic regulators SnRK1 and TOR to govern immunity by differential phosphorylation of NPR1
papers.abstract: The immune signal SA triggers metabolic changes to activate SnRK1 while inhibiting TOR. These central metabolic kinases antagonistically phosphorylate the key immune regulator NPR1, thereby coupling cellular metabolic state to systemic acquired resistance.

papers.title: Influenza vaccine format mediates distinct cellular and antibody responses in human immune organoids
Aire is a cell-intrinsic regulator of natural IgM-secreting cells
papers.abstract: The autoimmune regulator (Aire) promotes T cell tolerance through promiscuous gene expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells, but growing evidence suggests that it has functions beyond its canonical role in thymic tolerance. Sayed et al. demonstrate that Aire acts as a cell-intrinsic regulator of T-independent natural IgM-secreting cells, homeostatically restraining their number and natural IgM abundance.

papers.title: Beyond BMI: The diet-microbiome context of the obesity paradox
papers.abstract: In Nature, Desharnais et al. show that in diverse mouse models, anti-PD-1 sensitivity is more closely linked to diet-microbiome-metabolite ecosystem than to obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction. Their findings reinforce body mass index (BMI) as an incomplete proxy for host biology and suggest strategies to improve anti-PD-1 efficacy without inducing obesity.

papers.title: Lysophospholipase PNPLA7 is a critical checkpoint of phosphatidylcholine catabolism and turnover for skeletal muscle homeostasis
papers.abstract: Matsumoto and Seo et al. demonstrate that the conversion of lysophosphatidylcholine to glycerophosphocholine by the lysophospholipase PNPLA7 is essential for skeletal muscle health. Global or muscle-specific deletion of PNPLA7 impairs phospholipid turnover, leading to skeletal muscle degeneration with mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: Daily briefing: Vaping has ‘alarming’ risks for children
Gut microbiota primes stroke severity via the AHR in intestinal dendritic cells
papers.abstract: Indole-producing Escherichia coli worsens ischemic stroke through the activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in dendritic cells. Limiting AHR signaling in DCs promotes gut-derived DC migration to the meninges, expands meningeal regulatory T cells, and reduces neuroinflammation. This microbiota-AHR axis offers a promising therapeutic target.

papers.title: Spatial evolution of a cachexia-promoting microenvironment in pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer cachexia is accompanied by progressive assembly of a spatially organized tumor-macrophage-fibroblast niche. Reciprocal signaling among the cellular populations in the niche is associated with muscle wasting and cachexia progression.

papers.title: Microbiome signatures linked to cancer and treatment adverse events in a real-world cohort
papers.abstract: In a large, real-world mixed-cancer cohort, analyses accounting for comorbidities and additional confounders indicate that most microbiome alterations are shared across cancers rather than specific to individual cancers. Distinct associations are limited to a subset of cancers and, in separate analyses, to age of onset and specific treatment-related adverse events.

papers.title: Microglia with distinct origins and non-canonical phenotypes coexist within the border-like niche of the brain’s circumventricular organs
papers.abstract: Circumventricular organs are specialized brain regions lacking a blood-brain barrier. Van Hove et al. reveal that these regions harbor unique microglia and border-associated macrophage populations that respond to ageing and metabolism and are partly derived from fetal monocytes entering during a perinatal window, which can fully adopt the microglia identity.

papers.title: Transcription factor clusters enhance gene expression in vivo without modulating bursting dynamics
papers.abstract: Cadar et al. show that the transcription factor Dorsal forms clusters at genes carrying many binding sites in living fly embryos. Losing these clusters is lethal, yet they do not switch genes on; they merely boost output from already-active genes, challenging prevailing views of how condensates control transcription.

papers.title: The early RNA decay factor ZC3H18 directs first intron splicing
papers.abstract: Le Rest et al. identify ZC3H18 as the long-sought molecular link between the cap-binding complex (CBC) and first intron splicing. ZC3H18 recruits early splicing factors through interactions that are mutually exclusive with RNA decay factor binding, implying how cap-bound nascent transcripts are directed toward productive splicing rather than degradation.

papers.title: Cargo crosslinking nucleates AP-1 lattice formation
papers.abstract: Cargo has traditionally been viewed as a passive substrate of coat-mediated transport. Cryo-EM reveals that cargo containing tandem sorting motifs directly promotes higher-order adaptor assembly by bridging AP-1 complexes, enabling efficient trafficking and neuronal development in zebrafish.

papers.title: Non-invasive control of gene editing in vivo by photoswitchable Cas12f and focused ultrasound
papers.abstract: Remote activation of a single-AAV-deliverable photoswitchable Cas12f system enables precise spatial and temporal control of genome editing in deep tissues without surgery or implanted devices.

papers.title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy
papers.abstract: Gut microbial taxonomy alone is a poor predictor of CAR-T cell therapy outcome. Instead, specific gut immunomodulatory metabolites exert opposing effects on CAR-T cell function and tumor control, identifying microbial metabolism as a potential target to predict and improve CAR-T cell outcomes.

papers.title: The wu wei of brain metastases: When the gift of a pause is also a vulnerability
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, García-Gómez et al. show that brain-seeding cancer cells exploit an MXD4-dependent proliferative pause that enables survival under stress before metastatic outgrowth. By restraining MYC and activating protective stress responses, this pause becomes an Achilles’ heel, potentially targetable to eradicate micrometastases before clinical relapse.

papers.title: A transient MXD4-dependent proliferative pause enables survival of brain micrometastases
papers.abstract: García-Gómez et al. identify a transient state, termed the proliferative pause, that enables the survival of micrometastases during vascular co-option by buffering organ-imposed stress. Targeting vulnerabilities associated with this state suppresses metastatic progression and relapse, revealing opportunities for preventive intervention.

papers.title: ATM safeguards DNA replication by restraining pathological repriming at endogenous base lesions
papers.abstract: Sommerova et al. show that ataxia telangiectasia-mutated (ATM) protects replicating cells by restraining pathological bypass of endogenous oxidative base lesions through PRIMPOL-mediated repriming. When ATM is lost, post-replicative adducted ssDNA gaps accumulate, creating dependence on homologous recombination for repair and driving PARP hyperactivation and PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

papers.title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex
papers.abstract: In-cell cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) combined with proteomics, integrative structural modeling, and bioinformatics enables discovery and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins. In the minimal bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae, this reveals a complex that links Sec-based protein translocation and extracellular folding, capable of supporting both co- and post-translational pathways.

papers.title: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries
papers.abstract: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) resolves and quantifies an almost complete view of bacterial translation, revealing how gene expression machineries coordinate across the processes of transcription, translation, and membrane engagement directly within a minimal bacterium.

papers.title: Resident tissue macrophages transfer selenium transporter protein to protect pancreatic cancer from ferroptosis
papers.abstract: Resident tissue macrophages establish a selenium-rich niche at the pancreatic tumor border and protect invading tumor cells from ferroptosis by transferring Selenop protein to EMThi cancer cells.

papers.title: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration
papers.abstract: APOE4 causes a pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition that promotes cerebrovascular fibrosis and perivascular amyloid accumulation. TGF-β inhibition reverses this pathological remodeling and thus presents a therapeutic strategy to restore cerebrovascular homeostasis in these high-risk individuals.

papers.title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation
papers.abstract: Mammalian embryos see a substantial increase in available oxygen once the placenta forms. This increase in oxygen exposure serves as a trigger for initiating the development of the hindlimb, thus controlling developmental timing and, more broadly, linking the maternal environment to evolutionary changes in body plan.

papers.title: Targeting a site of vulnerability on circumsporozoite protein inhibits Plasmodium vivax malaria infection
papers.abstract: Limited knowledge of protective B cell epitopes on the Plasmodium vivax circumsporozoite protein (PvCSP) remains a roadblock to vaccine development. Visweswaran et al. identify an inhibitory vaccine epitope on PvCSP that elicits antibodies capable of blocking sporozoite invasion of host hepatocytes. Definition of the structural basis for epitope recognition by a neutralizing antibody provides a roadmap for vaccine design.

papers.title: Human-centric preclinical models for CAR T cell therapy in solid tumors: Where patient-derived organoids fit
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has shown promising activity in solid tumors, yet translational progress remains limited by preclinical models that incompletely capture human tumor biology. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) preserve key features of human tumors, including cellular heterogeneity and tissue architecture, thereby enabling functional evaluation of CAR T cell targets, next-generation approaches, resistance mechanisms, and selected safety considerations. We discuss how PDOs complement existing preclinical platforms to support CAR T cell development for solid tumors.

papers.title: Simplifying in silico protein evolution with minimal screening by unZipro
papers.abstract: Qin et al. present unZipro, a geometric deep learning framework that adapts general protein design models to specific protein families. By leveraging meta-learning, unZipro efficiently navigates family-specific fitness landscapes, enabling rapid protein evolution across gene editing, luciferase reporting, transcriptional regulation, and antiviral resistance with minimal experimental screening.

papers.title: Vast cellular gene-expression atlas could transform how scientists understand brain ageing and disease
Microbial signaling coordinates group oviposition and predator defense in migratory locusts
papers.abstract: This study reveals an egg-associated bacterial signaling mechanism that couples reproductive synchronization with offspring defense in the locust L. migratoria, expanding the functional landscape of insect-microbe-predator interactions and demonstrating how microbial signals can shape complex ecological behaviors.

papers.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons can infect neighboring cells using a mechanism that relies on a small fusogen-like protein rather than on the envelope protein that is typically required for infection.

papers.title: Projection-defined modules reveal mouse motor cortex architecture
papers.abstract: The mouse motor cortex divides into 16 spatially organized modules based on distinct subcortical projections. This specificity covaries with cortical connectivity patterns and cell-type composition along two spatial axes, thereby defining the rules by which motor cortex modules integrate with granularity into brainwide and precisely wired neuronal networks to influence movement.

papers.title: CD4 T cells convert transient responses to KRAS inhibition to durable remissions in pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: An AI-designed IL-21 mimetic converts transient KRAS inhibitor responses into durable pancreatic cancer remissions through CD4 T cells, independent of CD8 T cells and tumor MHC class I expression.

papers.title: Germinal center interleukin-4 microniches drive tissue divergence of IgE memory B cell responses
papers.abstract: IgE recall responses sustain allergic disease, but their anatomical regulation remains poorly understood. Villazala-Merino et al. identify Tfh cell-derived IL-4 microniches within germinal centers as an anatomical checkpoint that favors IgE recall responses in lymphoid organs while limiting their generation in the lung mucosa.

papers.title: Switching of transcriptional control from interferon regulatory factor 2 to interferon regulatory factor 1 drives innate immune cell activation
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor signaling activates proinflammatory interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) even in the absence of interferon by triggering a shift from IRF2 to IRF1 occupancy at ISG promoters and enhancers. Newly translated IRF1 promotes proteasomal degradation of the weaker transcriptional activator IRF2 by engaging the E3 ubiquitin ligase SPOP.

papers.title: Sensory neuronal mTORC1 kinase signaling establishes neuroimmune memory that initiates allergic immunity
papers.abstract: How cumulative environmental allergen exposures are encoded by peripheral sensory neurons to shape immune responsiveness is unclear. Zhu et al. show that protease allergens induce an mTORC1-dependent, metabolically trained state in sensory neurons that amplifies later neuroimmune responses to allergens and enables cross-sensitization to antigenically distinct allergens.

papers.title: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway
papers.abstract: Cold-stress signals are transmitted to chloroplasts and subsequently trigger cold responses through an RAF-like bi-kinase module where cytoplasmic RAF3 and plasma membrane RAF6 translocate to chloroplasts, where they inhibit photosynthetic activity but activate nuclear cold-responsive gene expression.

papers.title: mRNA-encoding CD19-targeting T cell engager for refractory immune thrombocytopenia
papers.abstract: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle-encoded CD19×CD3 T cell engager depletes B cells with attenuated cytokine release in preclinical models. In three patients with treatment-refractory immune thrombocytopenia, treatment with this T cell engager achieved sustained platelet recovery over 6 months, suggesting that mRNA-encoded T cell engagers represent a promising therapeutic approach for resetting autoreactive immunity in B cell-driven autoimmune disease.

papers.title: γδ T cells BiTE back at small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Ng et al. characterize and leverage cytotoxic γδ T cells in small cell lung cancer to overcome unsuccessful checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. Engaging Vδ2+ cells with a bispecific T cell engager (BiTE) bypasses the challenge of low MHC-I expression and ineffective CD8+ T cells.

papers.title: γδ T cells modulate anti-tumor immunity in small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: Ng et al. show that γδ T cells infiltrate SCLC and have cancer-fighting abilities. These cells can be harnessed through multiple therapeutics to kill SCLC, including through MHC-independent recognition mechanisms via BTN2A1. Notably, γδ T cell infiltration is clinically relevant in SCLC, with high levels predictive of improved outcomes with αPD-L1.

papers.title: Toward autonomous science with agentic artificial intelligence
papers.abstract: Biomedical artificial intelligence is advancing from tools that answer human-posed questions to agents that ask their own. Guo et al. assess this transition, including scaling logic, autonomous-laboratory trajectory, and the risks of hallucination, bias, dual use, and cognitive deskilling. This perspective argues that progress depends on responsible human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery
papers.abstract: Phosphorothioates, stereospecific modifications of the RNA phosphate backbone in anaerobic archaea, expand the epitranscriptome beyond nucleobases and ribose sugars. Installed by Esti enzymes at conserved rRNA and tRNA hotspots, these environmentally responsive marks stabilize tRNAs and support growth at high temperatures.

papers.title: Cancers modulate processing and presentation of p53 neoantigens to evade T cell detection
papers.abstract: Mutations in TP53 occur early in malignant transformation and are generally present in all descendant tumor cells. Haratani et al. find a dearth of actionable neoantigens displayed in the cancer immunopeptidome and define various mechanisms whereby tumor cells prevent effective processing and presentation of p53 neoantigens.

papers.title: Myeloid reprogramming generates myeloid-derived activating cells to potentiate radiotherapy and suppress metastasis
papers.abstract: Ji et al. show that radiotherapy induces a TET2-dependent epitranscriptomic program in myeloid cells that promotes immunosuppressive M-MDSC differentiation. TET2 loss preserves caRNA m5C-MBD6 signaling, restores IRF3-IFN-I activation, generates myeloid-derived activating cells, and enhances radiotherapy-induced antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Beyond genes and hotspots: Protein-informed interpretation of cancer mutations
papers.abstract: Interpreting the biological and clinical significance of somatic mutations in cancer genomes remains challenging. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Hyeon et al. identify and map significantly mutated regions to protein domains and structural features, establishing a proteo-genomics framework for interpreting cancer mutations beyond genes and hotspots.

papers.title: 3D chromatin remodeling during domestication defines novel targets for crop improvement
papers.abstract: Population-level 3D genome atlas of 34 semi-wild and 267 cultivated allotetraploid cottons reveals domestication-selected chromatin conformations that enhance cotton fiber quality and unlock cryptic breeding targets.

papers.title: Chemotherapy-free phase 1/2 trial of HRS-4642 plus adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: Shi et al. report the first clinical study of the selective KRAS G12D inhibitor HRS-4642 combined with the anti-PD-L1 antibody adebrelimab in heavily pretreated patients with KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic cancer. The chemotherapy-free regimen demonstrates a manageable safety profile and preliminary antitumor activity, supporting its feasibility as a targeted strategy in this molecularly defined subset.

papers.title: Gliomas phenocopy an inborn error of metabolism to drive neuronal activity and tumor growth
papers.abstract: Glioma-derived guanidinoacetate depolarizes neighboring neurons through γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) A receptors, and depleting this metabolite reduces both neuronal activity and glioma growth.

papers.title: Single-cell-resolved genome atlas of prokaryoplankton inhabiting the ocean’s interior
papers.abstract: GORG-Dark presents genomes of 9,698 individual bacterial and archaeal cells from the ocean’s sunless interior. The atlas resolves depth stratification to abyssal waters, uncovers particle-attached Pelagibacterales, maps chemolithoautotrophy and biosynthetic gene clusters, and identifies a rhodopsin clade specific to the dark ocean.

papers.title: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting triggers translational stress to promote viral replication
papers.abstract: Viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 can use programmed ribosomal frameshifting to turn off host translation and promote viral replication, expanding the known uses of programmed ribosomal frameshifting by viruses.

papers.title: Chronotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors: The knowns, the unknowns, and the contested
papers.abstract: Emerging data indicate that immune checkpoint inhibitors can exhibit time-of-day-dependent effects in pre-clinical models. Furthermore, multiple retrospective clinical trials associate earlier anti-tumor treatment timing with improved outcomes. However, key questions remain regarding the reproducibility of these findings, the underlying mechanisms, and their clinical implications. This commentary discusses these open questions and provides an outlook on the field.

papers.title: 5-Azacytosine induces cytotoxicity via 5-methylcytosine depletion on chromatin-associated RNA in leukemia
papers.abstract: Gao et al. reveal that the clinically used drug 5-azacytidine (5-azaC) induces transcriptional repression through RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) depletion, rather than acting solely as a DNA hypomethylating agent. Loss of m5C disrupts both MBD6-mediated H2AK119ub removal and SRSF2-mediated H3K27ac deposition, triggering leukemia cell death via cell-cycle disruption and defective DNA repair.

papers.title: Norway spruce spatiotemporal programs of conifer reproductive development
papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics across conifer reproductive and vegetative shoots reveals candidate developmental regulators and evolutionarily conserved tissue patterning genes in seed plants.

papers.title: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis
papers.abstract: Copper binding drives MYH9 polymerization, triggering cytoskeletal collapse and cuproptosis. HThPA releases intracellular copper through glutathione depletion, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes
papers.abstract: Metax is a cross-domain metagenomic profiler that uses genome-wide coverage evidence to improve species-level microbial profiling and distinguish supported taxa from artifacts. Across diverse datasets, Metax enables robust taxonomic profiling, pathogen detection, contamination assessment, and discovery of disease-associated bacterial and viral signatures.

papers.title: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
papers.abstract: Cell-mediated immunity requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Here, D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) is shown to act as a metabolic adjuvant, driving the conversion of proliferating CD8+ T cells into cytotoxic effector cells by linking mitochondrial ATP production to chromatin remodeling and gene expression.

papers.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapy holds promise for reversal of bone loss in osteoporosis. This phase 1 study establishes the safety and feasibility of intravenous administration of glycocalyx-engineered human MSCs and provides evidence that MSCs derived from the bone marrow of older individuals with osteoporosis retain clinically meaningful osteoregenerative capacity.

papers.title: Architecture of the serotonergic projectome in the mouse brain
papers.abstract: Serotonin neurons innervate nearly the entire mammalian brain, yet how their projections are organized has remained unclear. Systematic whole-brain serotonergic axon collateralization mapping reveals five projectomic groups that preferentially target functionally related regions, with each projectomic group connecting to specific spatial transcriptomic and behavioral profiles.

papers.title: Teamwork makes the dream work? Ensemble learning in computational pathology
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Luo et al. report an ensemble approach that integrates five pretrained pathology foundation models into a slide-level representation to exploit their complementary information, yielding improvements in tumor subtyping, biomarker, and therapy-response prediction. This shows the potential of ensemble and multimodal approaches in computational pathology.

papers.title: Ensemble learning of pathology foundation models for precision oncology
papers.abstract: Luo et al. develop ELF, a framework that ensembles five pathology foundation models to generate unified representations from whole-slide images. Trained on nearly 54,000 slides across 20 anatomical sites, ELF outperforms individual foundation models in disease classification, biomarker detection, and prediction of response to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy.

papers.title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice
papers.abstract: Mutations accumulate in cells with age, while caloric restriction extends lifespan across diverse animals. Grońska-Pęski et al. study the effect of caloric restriction on mutations genome-wide in mice, finding reduced mutation burdens across several tissues and cell types, thereby establishing that diet can alter mutation accumulation genome-wide during aging.

papers.title: Effector differentiation by stem-like intraepithelial γδ T cells is required for host defense against infection
papers.abstract: (Immunity 59, 1–21.e1–e7; March 10, 2026)

papers.title: UniCure: A multi-modal model for predicting personalized cancer therapy response
papers.abstract: Chen et al. present UniCure, a multi-modal foundation model that predicts drug-induced transcriptomic responses across diverse cellular contexts. By bridging cancer cell line data with patient-derived models, UniCure enables personalized drug prioritization and patient stratification, with its predicted therapeutic rankings correlating strongly with clinical survival outcomes in real-world cohorts.

papers.title: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex
papers.abstract: Cryo-EM and genetic analyses reveal that the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler is an integral component of the transcription pre-initiation complex. The structures demonstrate how SWI/SNF facilitates transcription initiation through stabilization of PIC organization and concerted remodeling of the +1 nucleosome.

papers.title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans
papers.abstract: The tendon/ligament stem cell is identified, and dysregulation of differentiation in this cell is shown as a mechanism contributing to lumbar spinal stenosis.

papers.title: Twenty-year persistence of SARS-CoV-1 immune imprinting shapes antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Our understanding of long-term sarbecovirus immune imprinting remains limited. Zhang et al. reveal persistent imprinting in individuals sequentially infected with SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 over two decades, characterized by redirected antibody targeting from the variable receptor-binding motif to conserved receptor-binding domain (RBD) core regions after breakthrough infection. These findings define the durability and molecular basis of antibody imprinting and inform pan-sarbecovirus vaccine design.

papers.title: A pulmonary innate lymphoid cell-driven serotonergic neuroimmune axis orchestrates airway hyperreactivity and cough hypersensitivity
papers.abstract: ILC2s engage in bidirectional neuroimmune crosstalk that shapes diverse physiological functions, yet whether ILC2-mediated serotonergic signaling affects asthma pathophysiology remains unexplored. Luo et al. show that ILC2-derived serotonin promotes type 2 immunity and activates vagal sensory neurons, contributing to airway hyperreactivity, lung inflammation, and cough hypersensitivity upon RSV infection. These findings reveal an ILC2-neuron crosstalk in asthma pathophysiology.

papers.title: Retraction Notice to: Taxanes trigger cancer cell killing in vivo by inducing non-canonical T cell cytotoxicity
UV irradiation drives lineage-specific MITF-mediated transcription of PD-L1 to confer immune tolerance to UV-mutated melanocytes
papers.abstract: (Immunity 59, 2500–2514.e1–e8; September 8, 2026)

papers.title: Tabula Sapiens 2.0: A comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types
papers.abstract: An expanded atlas of human cells maps the expression of nearly all human transcription factors across 701 cell-type/tissue combinations and uncovers the heterogeneous nature of senescence across tissues and cell types.

papers.title: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host
papers.abstract: How do maternal gut bacteria seed the rapidly developing neonatal gut? Heo et al. show that Bacteroides fragilis produces a distinct membrane lipid that enables this strict anaerobe to tolerate a microaerobic environment. This finding highlights divergent evolutionary strategies among related species, most of which rely on lipids conferring broader fitness.

papers.title: Ratiometric transcriptional activation by protein degradation
papers.abstract: By tethering a protein of interest to anti-CRISPR, protein degradation is transformed into amplified and programmable transcriptional outputs via Cas-based transcription factors, with sensitivity to protein loss tuned by the anti-CRISPR-Cas ratio. These synthetic circuits can be multiplexed to enable high-throughput discovery of protein-degrading and -destabilizing molecules.

papers.title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles
papers.abstract: We developed an AI-based and principled computational strategy for de novo design of Rhobins, compact pan-rhodamine binders with high brightness, reversible binding, and extreme stability. It enables superior live-/fixed-cell, super-resolution, and single-molecule imaging with properties surpassing existing tags. It also supports extremophile imaging at 75°C, inaccessible with current tools.

papers.title: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits
papers.abstract: A dynamic atlas of gene regulation was generated by perturbing every expressed gene across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells under resting conditions and following re-stimulation. The resulting map reveals context-specific regulators of immune programs and links regulatory pathways to naturally occurring T cell states and autoimmune disease risk.

papers.title: Human nuclear ribomes reveal DNA-embedded ribonucleotides as epigenetic modulators of transcription-associated DNA supercoiling
papers.abstract: Human nuclear ribomes reveal that DNA-embedded ribonucleotides accumulate at promoter-associated regulatory elements and scale with transcriptional activity. RNase H2 and Top1 process these ribonucleotides to modulate DNA supercoiling, uncovering a previously unrecognized epigenetic mechanism underlying transcription.

papers.title: A distinct effector B cell population drives autoantibody production in SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Autoantibodies (autoAbs) are linked to mortality and Long COVID, yet their cellular origins remain unclear. Yuan et al. identify a distinct B cell population (DN2 cells) as a key source of autoAbs during SARS-CoV-2 infection. These cells mirror lupus DN2s and carry a strong autoimmune genetic signature, linking infection-triggered autoAbs to autoimmune predisposition and Long COVID.

papers.title: dsRNAscan maps human dsRNAome, revealing conservation, intermolecular dsRNA, and correlates of ADAR dependency
papers.abstract: Andrews and Bass develop dsRNAscan to predict millions of double-stranded RNA structures across the human genome. ADAR editing and structure-probing data classify ∼2.4 million predictions as high-confidence, enabling prediction of intermolecular dsRNAs, conserved dsRNAs, and quantification of dsRNA burden as a correlate of cell death after ADAR knockout.

papers.title: T cell fate is dictated by different antigen-presenting cells in response to dietary versus gut epithelial self-antigen
papers.abstract: Mechanisms governing T cell responses to food or microbes have been characterized; however, whether they also regulate gut autoimmunity is unknown. Zhou et al. uncover that self-antigens depend on distinct subsets of antigen-presenting cells compared with dietary antigens for tolerogenic and effector T cell responses. This translates into antigen-source dependent disease susceptibility.

papers.title: Long-lasting extracellular matrix modifications reshape intestinal stem cell fate and promote chronic inflammation
papers.abstract: Whether inflammation leaves a lasting imprint on the intestinal stem cell (ISC) niche has remained unknown. Adir et al. find that persistent modified ECM (modECM) encodes inflammatory memory, reshapes Lgr5+ ISCs into wound-associated epithelia, and promotes maladaptive regeneration, immune infiltration, and chronic inflammation. These pathological regenerative states are recapitulated in individuals with ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue
papers.abstract: Spatial Hi-C-RNA simultaneously maps genome architecture and gene expression from the same tissue, revealing how spatial genome organization shapes cellular identity, development, and tumor evolution beyond what transcriptomics alone can capture.

papers.title: Proteo-genomics-guided interpretation of somatic mutations in cancer genomes
papers.abstract: Hyeon et al. integrate protein structures with population-scale cancer genomics data to characterize significantly mutated regions in 173 cancer-relevant genes. These regions align with functional domains, three-dimensional structural constraints, and gene-specific biology, providing a framework for classifying mutation patterns in cancer genes and prioritizing sparsely annotated variants for clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Tumor cells recruit macrophage bodyguards to outlast chemotherapy
papers.abstract: In Cell Press Blue, Carvalho et al. identify spatially organized tumor-macrophage niches, EMT-like CD44high cancer cells paired with SPP1/PARP14high macrophages, that drive chemoresistance in bladder cancer. PARP14 inhibition can flip this protective niche into an inflammatory, cisplatin-sensitizing state.

papers.title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits
papers.abstract: Gut bacteria convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that distribute systemically and signal independently of free nitric oxide. These microbe-derived DNICs protect against cardiometabolic disease and fatty liver by restoring compromised metabolic signaling pathways.

papers.title: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo
papers.abstract: Genome-wide mapping of RNA structure in murine norovirus reveals structural elements whose disruption impairs viral replication in cells and in vivo. Such structural disruptions generate a genetically stable virus that elicits protective immunity in vivo, offering a rational strategy for RNA virus vaccine design.

papers.title: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan
papers.abstract: A multimodal single-nucleus atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei spanning eight macaque brain regions across the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals, reveals region-specific and shared patterns of cellular vulnerability during aging. This framework provides a basis for dissecting shared and divergent molecular programs underlying primate brain aging, longevity, and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Intratumoral Bacillus cereus orchestrates stem-like lymphoid niches to potentiate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: Hu et al. integrate spatial multi-omics to identify stem-like lymphoid niches (SLNs) organized by CD70+ ILC2s and Tpex cells that predict PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy responses in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). They reveal that Bacillus cereus-PI-PLC increases SLN abundance and synergizes with PD-L1 blockade, highlighting microbiota-driven enhancement of cancer immunotherapy through SLNs therapeutically in HCC.

papers.title: Ancient genomes reveal distinct human dispersals and social stratification in the settlement history of western Remote Oceania
papers.abstract: The peopling of Remote Oceania involved some of humanity’s greatest expansions into the open ocean. Ancient DNA spanning the last 3,000 years from the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga reveals the sources and timing of dispersals following the initial settlement and uncovers social practices of an early Fijian community that experienced recent Papuan-related gene flow.

papers.title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human
papers.abstract: This study identifies cMAF as a key transcription factor that orchestrates the molecular crosstalk between brain perivascular macrophages and arteries, thereby sustaining cerebrovascular function in health and disease.

papers.title: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation
papers.abstract: Functional profiling of ∼200,000 genomic segments from vertebrate-infecting viruses uncovers RNA elements that boost gene expression by stabilizing mRNAs and enhancing translation, revealing the diversity of TENT4-dependent mixed tailing and identifying canonical poly(A) polymerase-mediated cytoplasmic polyadenylation, together expanding our understanding of post-transcriptional regulation and RNA therapeutic design.

papers.title: The genesis of cutaneous neurogenic inflammation is a multi-step process requiring dendritic cell aggregation
papers.abstract: Neurogenic inflammation is an important component of cutaneous immunity, yet the mechanism remains incompletely defined. Chen et al. found that the neuropeptide substance P activates mast cell release of the chemokine CCL2 to form dermal aggregates of dendritic cells that are then efficiently activated by a second neuropeptide, CGRP⍺. Thus, initiation of neurogenic inflammation is a dynamic, multi-step process.

papers.title: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells activate myelin-reactive T cells to augment neuroinflammation
papers.abstract: The meninges play a key role in central nervous system (CNS) inflammation and autoimmunity, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Huang et al. find that group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) accumulate in the dura during neuroinflammation, where they activate and expand myelin-reactive T cells, thereby augmenting neuroinflammation and CNS demyelination. Conditional deletion of H2-Ab1 in ILC2s diminishes neuroinflammation and CNS demyelination, highlighting ILC2s as a potential therapeutic target for restricting neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Virus-induced deconjugation of ISG15 dysregulates innate immunity and cellular metabolism
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 encodes a viral deISGylase called PLpro, but its physiological functions and direct substrates remain elusive. Using a deISGylation-activity-ablated recombinant SARS-CoV-2, Zhu et al. show that deISGylation activity is required for innate immune evasion and, furthermore, relieves metabolic restriction of viral replication by modulating the activity of key enzymes in glycolysis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and redox homeostasis.

papers.title: Metabolic atlas of early human cortex reveals glycolytic remodeling and pentose phosphate pathway control of cell fate transitions
papers.abstract: The developing human cortex is composed of diverse cell types, but how nutrient metabolism shapes their fate has remained unclear. This study maps the metabolic landscape of the developing human cortex and identifies glycolysis and pentose phosphate pathway activity as key regulators of radial glia fate, controlling the generation of outer radial glia and inhibitory neurons.

papers.title: CD163+ red pulp macrophages interact with marginal metallophilic macrophages during blood-stage malaria to maintain splenic architecture
papers.abstract: Splenic macrophages adapt to malaria through subset-specific remodeling and inter-macrophage communication. Using fate mapping, single-cell transcriptomics, and genetic perturbation, Mauel et al. show that red pulp macrophages (RPMs) and marginal metallophilic macrophages (MMMs) are predominantly yolk sac derived. They identify a CD163high iron-recycling RPM subset that is lost after malaria and find that stress response factor GDF15-dependent signaling supports MMM maintenance.

papers.title: Milk osteopontin alters the infant microbiome to drive DC hematopoiesis and disease tolerance
papers.abstract: Milk-derived osteopontin confers protection from viral or bacterial severe lower respiratory illness by altering the neonatal gut microbiome.

papers.title: Co-option of retrotransposons promotes antibody diversification
papers.abstract: A longstanding mystery in antibody diversification is how AID specifically targets immunoglobulin V genes. Ancient LINE-1 retrotransposons embedded within the immunoglobulin locus provide a recruitment platform for the HUSH complex and AID to drive somatic hypermutation.

papers.title: Butyrophilin-like 3 and 8 tetramers clamp Vγ4Vδ1 T cell receptors for antigen-independent activation
papers.abstract: BTNL3 and BTNL8 are butyrophilin-like receptors that selectively regulate intestinal Vγ4+ T cells, yet the underlying activation mechanism has remained elusive. Dong et al. reveal that BTNL3-BTNL8 forms an antigen-independent tetramer that drives γδ TCR dimerization and activation, providing a structural basis for tissue-specific immune surveillance.

papers.title: Escaping our own biases: AI, scientific reasoning, and discovery in molecular biology
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence may transform molecular biology not by always providing the correct answer, but by exploring mechanistic possibilities unconstrained by the assumptions that shape expert thinking. Its greatest contribution may be exposing the intellectual blind spots of scientists, while experimental validation remains the ultimate arbiter of truth.

papers.title: CRISPR screens identify targets to rescue age-related T cell dysfunction in cancer
papers.abstract: Dusp5 and Zfp219 serve as critical regulators of age-related T cell dysfunction, with the loss of either driving T cells into an effector-like state that improves tumor control through distinct mechanisms within the aged tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: An Oryza orphan gene confers trans-species drought tolerance
papers.abstract: ROAD1 is an Oryza-specific orphan gene that co-opts conserved ABA signaling to enhance drought tolerance without obvious growth defects or yield penalty under normal conditions. Elite rice lines carrying its functional allele exhibited higher grain yield than controls under drought, and its heterologous expression enhanced drought tolerance across diverse angiosperms.

papers.title: Nasal immunity in respiratory viral infection, transmission, and protection
papers.abstract: The nasal mucosa is a key decision point during respiratory viral infection. Here, Kazer et al. review new understanding of how local host cell subsets respond during viral infection and how this knowledge may enable tissue-scale protection through mucosal vaccines.

papers.title: Author Correction: Ferroelectric ultraviolet photodetector material with ultrafast response speed
Neonatal overfeeding accelerates age-related sarcopenia and metabolic disorders through lifelong gut mucosa and microbiota programming in mice
papers.abstract: Early-life nutrition shapes lifelong health, yet the long-term consequences of childhood overnutrition, particularly on musculoskeletal aging, remain unclear. Here, we show that neonatal overfeeding acts as a developmental insult that accelerates age-related sarcopenia in both sexes. Using different mouse models, early overnutrition shortens lifespan and exacerbates late-life muscle atrophy, accompanied by metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, neonatal overfeeding disrupts goblet cell development, leading to persistent mucus barrier defects and consequently reduced Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila) colonization during aging. Fecal microbiota transplantation transfers the sarcopenic phenotype, implicating gut dysbiosis in disease propagation. Loss of A. muciniphila reduces acetate production, impairs muscle mitochondrial function at least in part via suppressed GPR43 signaling, and aggravates sarcopenia. Conversely, A. muciniphila reconstitution or acetate supplementation restores mitochondrial homeostasis and improves muscle performance in aged mice. These findings reveal a developmental origin of age-related sarcopenia and define a gut-muscle axis linking early-life overnutrition to muscle aging, highlighting the preventive potential of optimizing early nutrition to support healthy aging. Here, the authors demonstrate that neonatal overfeeding in mice shortens lifespan and accelerates late-life muscle loss. This originates from persistent gut mucus defects and depleted Akkermansia muciniphila, revealing a targetable developmental origin for sarcopenia.

papers.title: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are essential for maintaining immune homeostasis and preventing autoimmune diseases, but are also a major cellular constituent of the tumor microenvironment (TME) that facilitates cancer progression. Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to specifically disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs, without affecting Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis remain a challenge. Here, we report that expression of the chromatin-organizer protein special AT-rich sequence binding protein 1 (Satb1), in Tregs is critical for their tumor-promoting functions in the TME, but not strictly required to suppress inflammatory T cells in autoimmune colitis. Satb1 expression differentiated between two Treg subtypes with distinct display of Treg phenotypic markers in lymphoid organs. Using transfer experiments, we discovered a context-specific switch in Satb1 protein expression between the two Treg subtypes. In mice, Treg-specific deletion of Satb1 augmented TCF-1 expression via a signaling axis involving Stat3 and the RNA-binding protein poly(C)-binding protein 1 (PCBP1), impairing the activities of tumor-infiltrating Treg cells. Simultaneous deletion of Satb1 and PCBP1 in Tregs completely restored Treg pro-tumorigenic functions and abolished the potent antitumor immune responses observed in Satb1-deficient mice. Our results reveal a key mechanism that may safely and potently enhance antitumor immunity without causing systemic autoimmune diseases. Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs remains a challenge. Here, the authors report that Treg expression of SATB1 distinguishes pro-tumorigenic Tregs from Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals the heterogeneous landscape of innate lymphoid cells in zebrafish
papers.abstract: In this study, Cheng et al. delineate a comprehensive atlas of innate lymphoid cells in zebrafish, unraveling their tissue distribution and developmental origins, and demonstrating interleukin-2 receptor beta as a critical regulator for their immune activity.

papers.title: Development of inducible genetic systems to finely tune efficacy of InhA-targeting anti-tuberculous drugs
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading global health threat, especially due to multidrug-resistant strains. The first-line drug isoniazid (INH) and second-line drugs ethionamide (ETH) and prothionamide (PTH), are prodrugs that target the essential enoyl-ACP reductase InhA, a key enzyme involved in mycolic acid biosynthesis. Resistance to these drugs primarily arises from genetic mutations that inactivate the enzymatic function of their respective bioactivating enzymes. While the recent development of chemical boosters has shown promising results in restoring drug susceptibility in these mutants, genetic tools to dynamically modulate these pathways and fine-tune resistance could be extremely valuable to develop the next-generation of anti-InhA drugs. In this context, we leverage CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) to develop inducible and reversible genetic systems to fine-tune antibiotic susceptibility in Mycobacterium smegmatis (Msmeg) and Mtb. By using our CRISPRi-based approach we first generated an inducible inhA hypomorph, an essential target required for mycolic acid production and bacterial growth, therefore confirming that our method is fully functional. Then, we developed genetic tools to selectively target katG, ethA, and the transcriptional repressor ethR, in order to generate conditional hypomorphs with altered antibiotic susceptibility profiles. Antibiotic susceptibility assays confirmed that the conditional hypomorphs selectively displayed high-level resistance or hypervulnerability to INH or ETH upon CRISPRi induction. Altogether, this work establishes CRISPRi as a powerful genetic platform for selectively fine-tuning mycobacterial drug susceptibility, with potential applications in developing next-generation anti-TB therapies.
affiliations: Aix Marseille Univ, CNRS, LISM, IM2B, Marseille, France (corresponding author)

papers.title: Human FACT complex coordinates cohesin and transcription on chromatin
papers.abstract: The spatial organisation of eukaryotic genomes is critical for coordinating DNA-dependent processes such as transcription and replication. Cohesin contributes to this organisation by extruding chromatin loops; however, how cohesin achieves processive translocation along nucleosome-dense chromatin in vivo remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the histone chaperone FACT as a regulator of cohesin dynamics in human cells. We show that the FACT subunit SUPT16H colocalises and interacts with cohesin on chromatin. Depletion of FACT impairs cohesin translocation from its loading sites, leading to reduced chromatin looping and decreased boundary strength of topologically associating domains (TADs), as revealed by Hi-C. In addition, FACT depletion results in the accumulation of cohesin within gene bodies that are not engaged in loop formation, which is associated with reduced transcription. Importantly, degradation of cohesin in FACT-depleted cells restores transcriptional output, indicating that cohesin mislocalisation underlies this effect. Together, these findings demonstrate that FACT facilitates cohesin translocation along chromatin, promoting efficient loop extrusion while preventing its aberrant accumulation within transcribed regions. This work provides mechanistic insight into how chromatin structure modulates cohesin function to coordinate genome organisation with transcription in mammalian cells.
affiliations: MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences (corresponding author)

papers.title: Achieving near single-molecule sensitivity in separation-free protein detection using engineered kinetic proofreading
papers.abstract: Unlike nucleic acids, proteins cannot be directly amplified. Ultrasensitive detection must therefore couple efficient analyte-to-signal conversion with strong suppression of target-independent background. Consistently detecting ~100 molecules (below which Poisson sampling noise alone causes CV to exceed 10%) across protein targets in a format as scalable and accessible as PCR remains unsolved. Separation-based ultrasensitive immunoassays require target binding stable enough to survive stringent washing and are therefore constrained by wash-induced signal loss and, more fundamentally, the relative scarcity of exceptionally tight binders. Performance consequently varies across targets; detection limits below 1,000 molecules remain rare. Conventional separation-free proximity assays avoid washing but incur background from random probe collisions, with reported detection limits frequently exceeding 100,000 molecules. Here we introduce Successive Proximity Extension Amplification Reaction (SPEAR), a separation-free architecture in which autonomous engineered DNA nanodevices emulate biological kinetic proofreading. Two successive irreversible proximity-extension steps compound discrimination between analyte-dependent and background reactions, suppressing spurious signals while preserving efficient analyte-to-signal conversion. This design reduces reliance on high-affinity binders and enables sub-fM detection from 1 uL samples through simple 3-step mixing followed by standard qPCR readout. Across 11 biomarkers tested, SPEAR consistently achieved sub-100-molecule detection limits. Where compared, it outperformed ultrasensitive separation-based platforms, analytically and clinically, including for low-abundance Alzheimer's disease biomarkers. SPEAR also precisely quantified SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody titers from finger-prick dried blood spots, concordant with the cell-based reference assay on venous blood. It detected a distinct mixed phosphorylation state of Tau, and targeting this state resolved previously observed capillary-venous discordance and improved amyloid-status discrimination. These results establish engineered autonomous successive molecular discrimination as a practical strategy for near-single-molecule protein detection, extending the sensitivity, scalability and accessibility of PCR-based testing to non-amplifiable analytes.
