Defining the native niche of pre-HSCs has also been hindered by their rarity, transient nature and lack of a single definitive marker for their identification in situ. Here, we integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to construct a spatiotemporal atlas of the niche in the AGM. Neural cells and chondrogenic mesenchyme predominated dorsally, whereas N-cadherin mesenchymal stromal cells (N-cad+ MSCs) formed a ventral layer between the aortic endothelium and mesonephric cells. BMP and SHH signaling showed overall dorsal enrichment, whereas WNT, NOTCH and KIT signaling were enriched ventrally, with these cellular and signaling patterns dynamically remodeled across HSC ontogeny. Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics validated the findings and further enabled the identification of individual pre-HSCs in situ and revealed a multicellular niche comprising endothelial cells, N-cad+ MSCs, intra-aortic hematopoietic cluster cells and macrophages. TGF{beta} and NOTCH signals were primarily supplied locally, whereas major sources of BMP and WNT were more distant. Functional perturbation identified niche-derived CD200 as an immune-regulatory signal promoting HSC development, validating a spatially predicted niche interaction. Together, our findings link tissue-scale spatial organization with the local multicellular niche supporting the preferential development of HSCs along the ventral aorta.
affiliations: Stowers Institute for Medical Research, Kansas City, MO 64110, USA. (corresponding author)

papers.title: Tropomodulin and Leiomodin Differentially Nucleate Tropomyosin Assembly on Actin Filaments
papers.abstract: Tropomyosins play a central role in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton by assembling along filaments into rope-like, head-to-tail polymers ("clusters") along filaments that regulate the binding and activity of numerous actin-binding proteins. Importantly, in cells, tropomyosins do not decorate actin filaments uniformly; some filaments are devoid of tropomyosins, whereas others recruit specific isoforms. To explore the diversity of tropomyosin-isoform binding kinetics and identify factors that control their assembly, we designed tropomyosin constructs, bearing a natural N-terminal acetylation and targeted cysteine mutations for fluorescence labelling. We analysed the binding of different tropomyosin isoforms to individual actin filaments reconstituted inside a microfluidic chamber. We show that, despite significant differences in spontaneous nucleation and elongation rates, all tested tropomyosin isoforms can coassemble within the same clusters. In addition, we identified tropomodulin and leiomodin, two pointed-end-binding proteins, to efficiently nucleate the formation of tropomyosin clusters on actin filaments, for all tested tropomyosin isoforms. Notably, while tropomodulin nucleates tropomyosin clusters from the pointed end, leiomodin does so along the entire filament.
affiliations: Institut Jacques Monod - CNRS (corresponding author)

papers.title: From Network Topology to Parameterization: An Optimized Model of Endothelial Mechanobiology
papers.abstract: Endothelial cells integrate biomechanical and biochemical cues to regulate vascular function, which can be modeled using cell signaling networks. Yet, the extent to which their signaling behavior is determined by network topology versus reaction-specific parameterization remains unclear. We developed a continuous logic-based ordinary differential equation model of vascular endothelial signaling containing 70 species and 123 regulatory reactions assembled from the literature. Model predictions were evaluated against 78 literature-defined directional responses to increased wall stress, wall shear stress, hypoxia, and TNF. We first tested whether a single global parameter triplet describing reaction weight (w), Hill coefficient (n), and half-maximal activation (EC50) could reproduce these observations. Investigator-selected global parameters reproduced 62 of 78 responses (79.49%). Monte Carlo sampling of 100,000 globally constant parameter sets improved agreement to 69 of 78 responses (88.46%), indicating that network topology alone captured most qualitative signaling behavior but remained sensitive to parameter choice. Allowing reaction-specific parameters increased the best agreement to 75 of 78 responses (96.15%). We then used a genetic algorithm to identify the smallest subset of reactions requiring reaction-specific specification while retaining a common constant-parameter spine for the remainder of the network. Complete agreement (100%) with all 78 literature-defined responses was achieved with reaction-specific parameterization of only 10 of 123 reactions. The optimized model was subsequently used to simulate continuous changes in wall shear stress, revealing pathway-dependent nonlinear responses, including monotonic increases in nitric oxide and pSmad1/5, nonmonotonic responses in endothelin-1 and NF-{kappa}B, and a biphasic pSmad2/3 response. These findings show that most observed endothelial signaling behavior can be reproduced by a fixed network topology with broadly shared reaction parameters with only a limited subset of interactions requiring quantitative specialization. This framework provides a compact endothelial signaling model for investigating mechanobiological regulation and for future integration with multiscale models of vascular adaptation and disease.
affiliations: Yale University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Colocalization between bone loading and metabolic activity in the human tibia in response to acute exercise
papers.abstract: Bone strain and remodeling are important factors for bone health. Improved characterization of relationships between these factors in response to acute loading will improve our understanding of bone maintenance, adaptation to load, and pathophysiology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate colocalization between finite-element-estimated bone strain and [18F]sodium fluoride positron emission tomography imaging-estimated subchondral bone remodeling in the tibial diaphysis in response to acute exercise. We hypothesized that the exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values would be greatest in regions of higher strain. 26 participants underwent bilateral positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance scans before and after a bout of stair ascent and descent exercise. Finite element analysis was performed to calculate principal strain distributions in the tibial diaphysis. [18F]sodium fluoride standardized uptake values were calculated from pre- and post-exercise positron emission tomography data and mapped to the tibial surface. Mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values were calculated and compared between regions defined by strain percentile. Both normalized mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values increased with maximum principal strain in a pattern suggesting an exponential relationship. Pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in standardized uptake value were notably much greater in the region of highest maximum principal strains (estimated marginal means = 76.9 and 71.0 percentile, respectively) when compared to all other regions of the tibial diaphysis ([≤] 61.1 and [≤] 57.0 percentile, respectively, p < 0.001). This study is the first to directly show a relationship between bone mechanical loads and acute [18F]sodium fluoride uptake in humans in vivo. Our results highlight the influence of tensile strain magnitude on bone metabolic activity in response to acute loading. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of a combined finite element analysis and positron emission tomography approach to interrogate relationships between bone loading and bone metabolic response to acute exercise.
affiliations: Stanford University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Bottom-up engineering of EV-mimetic vesicles reveals selective protein loading and modulates cellular uptake and biodistribution
papers.abstract: Biological systems such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) are highly sophisticated and functionally diverse. Despite growing recognition of EVs' roles in health and disease through mediating intercellular communication, their inherent heterogeneity and challenges in purity and yield hinder their mechanistic research and clinical translation. To address this gap, we sought to translate essential EV properties into a controllable and simplified platform by engineering biomimetic synthetic vesicles (SVs) incorporating defined proteins and lipids. Using microfluidics, we generated SVs loaded with bulk membrane and cytosolic proteins from cancer cells, as well as individual organotropism-associated integrins. Bulk membrane protein incorporation into SVs reduced surface charge, modified lipid profiles, and enhanced cellular uptake, while integrin incorporation altered biodistribution. To investigate protein loading, we profiled input materials and SVs by mass spectrometry, identifying features linked to high incorporation, such as low molecular weight, positive charge, high isoelectric point, and predicted stability, globularity, lipidation, and amphipathic helices. This work presents a synthetic platform for dissecting the roles of EV-associated features and cargo, while providing insights into protein properties relevant to the optimization of delivery systems.
affiliations: Cancer Research Program, Research Institute of the McGill University Health Centre, Montreal, QC, Canada (corresponding author)

papers.title: PyMOL plugin for Protein Circuit Topology
papers.abstract: Circuit Topology (CT) provides a fundamental framework for analysing folded polymer chains, with applications in functional annotation, protein engineering and drug development. We present a protein CT analysis plugin for PyMOL v3.1.6.1 with a graphical user interface (GUI), automatic installation, and novel features developed through integration with PyMOL's application programming interface (API). The plugin integrates various previously developed CT methodologies for studying structured proteins and their complexes as well as the dynamics of disordered proteins. Analysis of a representative protein and a molecular dynamics trajectory demonstrates the plugin's three analysis modes and their outputs. The plugin reproduces the reference ProteinCT implementation exactly on the structures tested, and is distributed with a versioned release, a pinned environment and a one-command reproduction of every static result reported here.
affiliations: Leiden University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Mechanophenotype of synovial fibroblasts correlates with patients' pathotypes and treatment response in Rheumatoid Arthritis
papers.abstract: The mechanical features of synovial fibroblasts may encode clinically relevant information for the management of rheumatoid arthritis. Indeed, it remains poorly understood the links between cellular and microenvironment mechanics with patient stratification and therapeutic response. Here we show that combining organotypic synovial cultures with multimodal mechanophenotyping and transcriptomics identifies distinct ''soft'' and ''stiff'' fibroblast states. Healthy and rheumatoid arthritis fibroblasts were cultured in two or three dimensions (organotypic cell cultures), alone or with endothelial cells, and characterized by high-throughput nanoindentation, picobalance measurements, digital holographic microscopy, Brillouin microscopy and RNA sequencing. Three-dimensional culture reduced single-cell Young's modulus and total mass while increasing dry-mass surface density; endothelial co-culture increased fibroblast stiffness and the longitudinal modulus of intact organotypic cultures. Stiffness-based grouping revealed transcriptional programmes related to extracellular-matrix remodelling, cytoskeletal contractility, and TGF-beta, WNT, and Hippo signalling. Mapping these signatures to publicly available rheumatoid arthritis clinical transcriptomic datasets associated the ''stiff'' state with fibrotic and myeloid-fibrotic pathotypes and treatment-refractory programmes, whereas the ''soft'' state aligned with lymphoid pathotypes and rituximab- or tocilizumab-responsive programmes. These findings support mechanophenotype-associated transcriptional signatures as potential biomarkers for rheumatoid arthritis stratification.
